breaking_changes: GET /api/v1/system-stats now reports the scalar gpu_percent and vram_gb fields for the primary GPU by total memory instead of the GPU with the highest utilization — on multi-GPU systems the numbers meaningfully change and existing dashboards or alerting based on those fields will see different values.

Models gated behind a guest-tier backend are now hidden from GET /v1/models?show_all=true and return model_not_supported on pull until the guest backend is installed — existing setups that relied on the model being visible without the backend will see them disappear.

checklist.text: Open the Lemonade website news page and confirm the AnythingLLM entry displays the correct title ('Why AnythingLLM is moving from Ollama to Lemonade and llama.cpp'), date (October 13, 2026), description, and that the link resolves to anythingllm.com.

evidence.blockers: Three P0 items: backend subprocess lifecycle (refactored start/stop/health), guest-backend model gating (new hidden-model behavior), and multi-GPU system-stats (changed primary-GPU selection). All require human verification on real hardware before release.
evidence.breaking_changes: The system-stats endpoint changed which GPU the scalar fields refer to (largest memory instead of highest utilization) — a behavioral change on multi-GPU systems. Guest-tier models are now hidden without their backend installed — a new gating behavior affecting model visibility and pull behavior.
evidence.coverage: All 15 to-dos from the 19 commit reviews are rated. Five commits had no to-dos (config path fix, shard dedup, Arch install docs, CI auto-labeler, pre-pull test infra). The remaining ten commits with to-dos are fully covered.
evidence.manual_testing: NPU hardware verification for FLM v1.0.8 and v1.0.9 (Fedora). Multi-GPU NVML system-stats on mixed NVIDIA/AMD and NVIDIA-only systems (Linux/Windows). Guest backend install on Strix Halo hardware. Multi-reference image editing endpoint with real images. All are unexercised in CI due to hardware requirements.
evidence.security: No security concerns identified across the release. The NVML DLL load path was hardened in this bucket (LOAD_LIBRARY_SEARCH_SYSTEM32 on Windows). No new credential handling, external network calls, or supply-chain risks beyond routine backend version bumps.
